title: Grade 5 Science — Properties and Changes of Matter
subject: Science
description: Practice with questions on mass, volume, mixtures, dissolving.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: Which tool can measure the mass of a sample?
Which property describes how much space an object takes up?
A stone raises the water level from 30 mL to 42 mL. What is the stone's volume?
Which substance is most likely to dissolve in water?
How could you separate sand from water?
choices: pour the mix through a filter
put the mixture in a closed jar

questions.question: After sugar dissolves in water in a sealed container, what happens to the total mass?
choices: It becomes the mass of sugar alone.

questions.question: Which property can help separate iron filings from dry sand?
What can happen to salt when salt water evaporates?
Which example involves a new substance forming?
Which is a change of state without a new substance forming?
What property lets you compare how easily samples are scratched?
Which would be best to compare the volume of two liquids?
Which observation shows that air takes up space?
choices: Air blown into a balloon makes it larger.

questions.question: Which example is a mixture rather than a single substance?
choices: sand and small pebbles mixed together

questions.question: Which setup tests whether warming water changes how fast sugar dissolves?
choices: Use more sugar only in the warm water.
Use equal sugar and water amounts at two temperatures.
Observe both for different amounts of time without recording.

questions.question: A cup of water changes to ice in a closed container. What happens to its total mass?
choices: It decreases because ice is cold.

questions.question: Which property helps you sort pebbles with a mesh screen?
A metal spoon is shiny. What kind of observation is that?
Which result supports the claim that a gas formed during a reaction in liquid?
choices: Bubbles appeared as the materials reacted.
The liquid turned solid before mixing.
The spoon used for stirring was long.

questions.question: Which pair could have equal volumes but different masses?
choices: two identical cubes of the same material
same-size blocks made of wood and metal
equal drops from one glass of water
two drops from the same oil sample with equal size
